# MAgPIE

## Overview

The Model of Agricultural Production and Its Impact on the Environment (MAgPIE) is a global food and land system modelling framework. It uses a wide range of spatially-explicit biophysical and socioeconomic information to model global land-use dynamics throughout the 21st century. MAgPIE operates at two spatial scales that include a coarse scale of twelve model regions with similar socioeconomic characteristics and a subregional level that combines biophysical information, such as suitability for agricultural production (crop yield potential, irrigation water requirements, travel time to urban markets etc.), to determine the cost-effectiveness of different land-use activities. Both these resolutions, however, are typically too coarse to assess how global land-use dynamics could drive landscape-scale changes and associated changes in biodiversity and ecosystems service supply, which is a key sustainability challenge.

The Spatial Economic Allocation Landscape Simulator (SEALS) model can therefore be applied to spatially allocate projected land-use dynamics to a spatial scale that is relevant for assessing landscape and biodiversity change. SEALS uses empirically calibrated adjacency relationships, physical suitability and conversion eligibility information at a spatial resolution of 300 x 300 Meter to allocate land use activities across space.

This tutorial describes how MAgPIE and SEALS are coupled. The coupling is run from the MAgPIE side through the output script `scripts/output/extra/runSEALSallocation.R`: after a MAgPIE run, the script prepares all SEALS inputs and starts the SEALS allocation. The tutorial assumes some familiarity with the MAgPIE model, in particular how to set up model runs. Basic tutorials on how to run the MAgPIE model can be found at <https://magpiemodel.github.io/tutorials.html>. The model documentation is published per release under `https://rse.pik-potsdam.de/doc/magpie/<version>/`. Use the version that matches your MAgPIE code (the `version` field in `CITATION.cff` of your MAgPIE folder); the newest release is listed at <https://github.com/magpiemodel/magpie/releases/latest>. For example, the documentation of release 4.14.1 is at <https://rse.pik-potsdam.de/doc/magpie/4.14.1/>.

## Getting MAgPIE itself running

Orientation notes for setting MAgPIE up, if you have not run it before. The
MAgPIE tutorials linked above are the authoritative source; these are the points
worth knowing before you start.

- Clone the development branch:

```
git clone -b develop https://github.com/magpiemodel/magpie.git magpie_develop
```

- The `input` and `output` folders are in `.gitignore`.
- MAgPIE has a config folder. `default.cfg` in it is very large, so rather than
  editing it directly, use a start script that reads lines from the default and
  overwrites the ones it needs.
- Start scripts live in the (non-ignored) `scripts/start` folder, for example
  `test_runs.R`.
- To run GAMS, see `scripts/start_functions.R`.

## How the coupling works

For each MAgPIE run, `extra/runSEALSallocation.R` performs the following steps:

1. **Gridded land use for SEALS.** It converts the disaggregated land-use shares `cell.land_0.5_share.mz` (written by `extra/disaggregation.R`) into the NetCDF file `cell.land_0.5_SEALS_<run title>.nc` in the MAgPIE run folder. The file contains the 2020 base year and the years in `cfg$seals_years` (default `c(2020, 2050)`).
2. **Scenario-specific SEALS inputs.** It reads two templates that are part of the MAgPIE input data (`input/` folder of the MAgPIE directory):
   - `seals_scenario_config.csv`: the SEALS scenario definitions, with a `Baseline` row and one scenario row.
   - `seals_global_coefficients.csv`: the SEALS model coefficients, including regressors specific to MAgPIE scenarios (`land_conservation`, `peatland_rewetting`, `snv20_realloc`, `snv20_expan`).

   It adapts both to the settings of the MAgPIE run and writes them to `output/seals/input/` as `seals_scenario_config_<run title>.csv` and `seals_global_coefficients_<run title>.csv`:
   - The scenario row gets the run title as label, the SSP from `c09_pop_scenario`, the RCP from the cellular input data, the years from `cfg$seals_years`, and the paths to the NetCDF file and the coefficient file.
   - Runs whose title contains `default`, `bau` or `SSPx-Ref` are treated as business-as-usual (`bau`), all others as `policy` runs that SEALS compares against `bau`.
   - Land conservation: the `land_conservation` regressor, which prevents agricultural expansion in protected areas, uses the protection layer of `c22_protect_scenario`, or of `c22_base_protect` if no protection scenario is set (e.g. `magpie_WDPA.tif`, `magpie_30by30.tif`).
   - Semi-natural vegetation: if `s29_snv_shr` is 0.2, the `snv20_realloc` regressor sets an incentive for the allocation of forest and other natural vegetation and `snv20_expan` constrains cropland expansion, following the semi-natural vegetation (SNV) policy of the MAgPIE run. Other values of `s29_snv_shr` cannot be represented at the 1 x 1 km scale and trigger a warning.
   - Peatland rewetting: if MAgPIE rewets more than 1 % of the peatland area, the `peatland_rewetting` regressor discourages agricultural expansion on peatlands and favours forest and other natural vegetation there.
3. **SEALS run file.** It reads the standard SEALS run file `seals/run_seals.py` from your SEALS code base and writes a copy `output/seals/scripts/run_seals_<run title>.py` in which the project directory (`output/seals`), the base data directory and the scenario definitions file are set. The project runs with `run_mode='check'`, so all MAgPIE runs share one SEALS project and reuse its prepared input data.
4. **SEALS allocation.** It starts SEALS either as a SLURM job or directly on the local machine (see [Execution modes](#execution-modes)).

## Setup

You need:

- A Python environment with SEALS and its dependencies (see [Installation](installation.qmd)).
- A local clone of the SEALS code (this repository). The coupling script uses `seals/run_seals.py` from it.
- A base data directory. SEALS checks it for all required data and downloads anything that is missing, so it can be empty on first use.

Then set the user settings at the top of `scripts/output/extra/runSEALSallocation.R`:

```r
### Name of the conda environment with SEALS installed
# see https://justinandrewjohnson.com/earth_economy_devstack/installation.html
# for instructions on how to set up a python environment for SEALS
sealsEnv <- "seals_2-1-1"

### SEALS base data folder, i.e. the folder named "base_data" (contains seals/, lulc/, ...).
### SEALS downloads missing base data into it
dirBaseData <- "<path/to/seals/files>/base_data"

### SEALS code clone, i.e. the folder that contains seals/run_seals.py
dirSEALS <- "<path/to/seals/files>/seals/seals_2-1-1"

### Where SEALS runs: "auto" (SLURM if available, else local), "slurm" (one job
### per scenario) or "local" (scenarios run one after another on this machine)
sealsMode <- "auto"
```

The example assumes the SEALS files are kept in one folder, `<path/to/seals/files>`, with the base data in `base_data/` and a clone of SEALS v2.1.1 in `seals/seals_2-1-1/`, and a conda environment named after the SEALS version. Adapt the paths to where your files are; `dirSEALS` must point to the folder that contains `seals/run_seals.py`. On Windows, use forward slashes, e.g. `"C:/Users/<username>/seals/files/base_data"`.

The SEALS scenario and coefficient templates do not need to be set up by hand; they come with the MAgPIE input data.

## Running the coupling

Add `"extra/runSEALSallocation"` to the output scripts in your start script, after `"extra/disaggregation"` (the order of the vector determines the order of execution):

```r
cfg$output <- c("output_check", "extra/disaggregation", "rds_report", "extra/runSEALSallocation")
```

and set the years to be allocated by SEALS:

```r
cfg$seals_years <- c(2020, 2050)
```

Alternatively, start the coupling for finished runs from the MAgPIE folder with

```
Rscript output.R
```

select the runs, then `extra` and `runSEALSallocation`, and finally the run submission type (e.g. `Direct execution`). The run folders must contain `cell.land_0.5_share.mz`, i.e. `extra/disaggregation.R` must have completed without error.

## Execution modes {#execution-modes}

With `sealsMode <- "auto"`, the script uses SLURM if the `sbatch` command is available and runs SEALS locally otherwise.

**SLURM (`"slurm"`).** Each MAgPIE run submits its own SEALS job (64 CPUs, qos `short`). The first job also prepares the input data shared by all runs and gets a time limit of 3 h. Its job ID is stored in `output/seals/seals.lock`. All later jobs depend on it (`--dependency=afterok`), reuse its input data and get a time limit of 40 min. If the first job failed, later submissions stop with an error; delete `seals.lock` to start the input data preparation again. The job settings (qos, partition, CPUs, conda activation via miniforge) are tailored to the PIK HPC cluster and may need to be adapted in `.submitSEALS()` for other clusters.

**Local (`"local"`).** SEALS runs in the R session that executes the output script, via `conda run -n <sealsEnv>`, so `conda` must be on the `PATH`. The R session waits until SEALS has finished. If several MAgPIE runs reach this step at the same time, a lock file (`output/seals/seals_local.lock`) makes them wait, so the SEALS allocations run one after another. The first allocation also prepares the input data and takes the longest; plan for several hours. The SEALS log of each run is written to `output/seals/scripts/outfile_local_<run title>.log`.

**Convolution cache.** In global runs, SEALS reads the simplified land cover map, the class binaries and their convolutions from `<dirBaseData>/lulc/esa/seals7/` if they exist there. Missing layers are computed in `output/seals/intermediate/fine_processed_inputs/lulc/esa/seals7/`. After a first run, the computed convolutions can be copied to the base data, so that later SEALS projects reuse them (2020 is the base year):

```bash
src=output/seals/intermediate/fine_processed_inputs/lulc/esa/seals7/convolutions/2020
dst=<dirBaseData>/lulc/esa/seals7/convolutions/2020
mkdir -p $dst && cp -n $src/*.tif $dst/
```

SEALS identifies these layers by file name only, and the names are the same for every ESA-to-seals7 correspondence. Copy only layers computed with the correspondence of the coupling (`esa_seals7_correspondence_mosaic-natural.csv`), because SEALS uses layers from another correspondence without an error. With `p.promote_lulc_layers_to_base_data = True` in the SEALS run file, SEALS copies the layers itself and records their correspondence in `<dirBaseData>/lulc/esa/seals7/provenance.json`. A later run with a different correspondence then rebuilds the layers in its own project. `runSEALSallocation.R` does not set this option.

### Notes for local runs

- **Python environment.** The editable installs of hazelbean and SEALS compile Cython extensions. On Windows this requires the Visual Studio Build Tools including the Windows SDK (e.g. "Windows 11 SDK"); without the SDK the build fails with `Cannot open include file: 'io.h'`.
- **Base data.** Everything SEALS needs must be in `dirBaseData` or downloadable from the SEALS cloud bucket. This includes the MAgPIE-specific regressors referenced in `seals_global_coefficients.csv` (e.g. `gpm2.tif`, `magpie_SNV20_realloc.tif`, `magpie_SNV20_expan.tif`, and the protection layers such as `magpie_BH.tif`), since SEALS loads every listed regressor. The precomputed convolutions (`lulc/esa/seals7/convolutions/<year>/`) also come from the bucket if missing. Copying a complete `base_data` from an existing setup (e.g. the cluster) avoids most downloads.
- **HTTPS interception.** Antivirus software or proxies that scan HTTPS traffic (e.g. Avast Web Shield) replace server certificates with their own root certificate. Python does not trust this root by default, so conda fails with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` and SEALS downloads from the bucket hang without an error message. Either exclude Python from HTTPS scanning, make Python use the Windows certificate store, or provide the required base data locally. If conda or mamba downloads time out, longer timeouts can help, e.g. `CONDA_REMOTE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS=60` and `CONDA_REMOTE_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS=120`.
- **Resources.** A global allocation needs a large share of a desktop machine's memory and CPU. Avoid other heavy processes while SEALS runs; the lock file only serialises the SEALS allocations themselves.
- **Log file on Windows.** The log file stays locked while SEALS runs and can only be opened after the run has finished.

## Outputs

All SEALS files are written to the SEALS project folder `output/seals` within the MAgPIE directory:

- `input/`: scenario definitions and coefficients per MAgPIE run
- `scripts/`: run files, SLURM output files and local log files
- `intermediate/stitched_lulc_simplified_scenarios/`: the allocated 300 m land-cover maps

## Reference: what the templates encode

This section documents the choices behind the MAgPIE templates, for users who want to adapt them. The columns of the scenario definitions are documented in [Custom scenarios](custom_scenarios.qmd).

**Land-type mapping.** MAgPIE separates seven land types, SEALS allocates changes for five. SEALS reads the mapping from the CSV file named in the scenario definitions (`coarse_correspondence_path`); the template uses `seals/default_inputs/magpie_seals7_correspondence.csv` in the base data directory. If the file is missing, or MAgPIE reports different land types, create it as follows:

1. List the land types in the MAgPIE NetCDF file. Each land type is a separate variable:

   ```r
   nc <- ncdf4::nc_open("output/<run folder>/cell.land_0.5_SEALS_<run title>.nc")
   names(nc$var) # "crop" "past" "primforest" "secdforest" "forestry" "urban" "other"
   ncdf4::nc_close(nc)
   ```

2. Write one row per variable:
   - `src_label`: the variable name, spelled exactly as in the NetCDF file. SEALS finds the land-type layers by this name.
   - `src_id`: any unique integer.
   - `dst_id` and `dst_label`: the SEALS class the land type is allocated to, one of `1 urban`, `2 cropland`, `3 grassland`, `4 forest`, `5 othernat`.
   - `src_description`, `dst_description`: free text, may be empty.

   ```r
   corr <- data.frame(
     src_id = 1:7,
     dst_id = c(2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 1, 5),
     src_label = c("crop", "past", "primforest", "secdforest", "forestry", "urban", "other"),
     dst_label = c("cropland", "grassland", "forest", "forest", "forest", "urban", "othernat"),
     src_description = c("cropland", "grassland", "primary forest", "secondary forest", "forestry", "urban land",
                         "non-forest vegetation"),
     dst_description = ""
   )
   ```

3. Save it under the path given in `coarse_correspondence_path`, relative to the base data directory:

   ```r
   write.csv(corr, file.path(dirBaseData, "seals/default_inputs/magpie_seals7_correspondence.csv"),
             row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
   ```

If you save it elsewhere, adapt `coarse_correspondence_path` in `input/seals_scenario_config.csv` of your MAgPIE folder accordingly.

**Base land cover.** The ESA CCI land-cover data overestimate the cropland extent. To better align it with the cropland initialisation in MAgPIE, the template uses `seals/default_inputs/esa_seals7_correspondence_mosaic-natural.csv`, which classifies "crop_natural_mosaic" as "othernat" and "natural_crop_mosaic" as "forest" instead of "cropland". The mapping corresponds to `esa_to_seals7_mosaic_is_natural_correspondence` in `seals/config.py`; SEALS reads it from the CSV file named in the scenario definitions (`lulc_correspondence_path`):

```
6,,30,2,crop_natural_mosaic,othernat
7,,40,2,natural_crop_mosaic,forest
```

**Policy regressors.** Constraints assumed in MAgPIE also need to hold during the downscaling. The multiplicative `land_conservation` regressor precludes the expansion of cropland and grassland in protected areas. `seals/static_regressors/magpie_WDPA.tif` contains legally protected areas from the WDPA database; layers for protection scenarios, such as `magpie_30by30.tif` for the 30x30 target of the Global Biodiversity Framework, contain both current protected areas and the areas protected under the scenario.

**Protected classes.** SEALS rewrites the rows named `<class>_constraint` in the coefficients for each run. Classes without a budget in the MAgPIE data (`water` and `other`) are protected automatically. A land-cover correspondence with a no-data class `ndv` makes SEALS stop, because `ndv` then counts as protected and the coefficients have no constraint row for it. The ESA correspondences in `seals/default_inputs/` have no such row. Urban has a budget and is protected only if the column `additional_protected_class_labels` in `input/seals_scenario_config.csv` contains `urban`. Because SEALS rewrites the `<class>_constraint` rows, a rule between two classes is stored in a separate multiplicative row of `seals_global_coefficients.csv`. The row `othernat_onto_forest` uses the forest map as layer and has a 0 in the `othernat` column, so othernat cannot expand onto forest.

**NetCDF only.** To create only the NetCDF file `cell.land_0.5_SEALS_<run title>.nc` without starting SEALS, use the output script `extra/reportMAgPIE2SEALS.R` instead.
